title: Analytical diagonalization of the open-boundary bosonic Kitaev chain: An asymmetric plane-wave ansatz approach
abstract: The bosonic Kitaev chain under open boundary conditions has attracted recent attention due to its realization in driven-dissipative systems and its intriguing non-Hermitian boundary physics. The model is known to be solvable via local squeezing transformations in the position-momentum representation. In this paper, we present an alternative, purely algebraic solution that relies entirely on the standard bosonic Bogoliubov transformation. For an $N$-site chain, we propose an asymmetric plane-wave ansatz with unequal left- and right-moving momenta to analytically solve the associated $2N\times 2N$ non-Hermitian ``associated matrix". The left eigenvalue problem yields $N$ distinct eigenvalues, each of which is twofold degenerate. By carefully resolving these degeneracies using the bosonic commutation relations, we construct the $N$ physical Bogoliubov quasiparticle operators. The construction reveals non-uniquenesses that in special cases exactly mirror the freedom in the local squeezing transformations of the original approach. The diagonal form of the Hamiltonian is obtained explicitly and is shown to be equivalent to the original Hamiltonian. The proposed asymmetric plane-wave ansatz and degeneracy-resolution technique are not limited to the present model and can be generalized to other bosonic pairing systems, including those with inhomogeneous pairing or hopping terms.
summary: This paper presents an alternative, purely algebraic method to diagonalize the open-boundary bosonic Kitaev chain by employing an asymmetric plane-wave ansatz. The technique solves the associated non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem and explicitly constructs the Bogoliubov quasiparticle operators. It demonstrates that this method is generalizable to other bosonic pairing systems with complex boundary conditions.
main_problem: The paper aims to analytically diagonalize the open-boundary bosonic Kitaev chain (OBKC) using a purely algebraic method that avoids the standard position-momentum representation.
main_result: The authors successfully derive the explicit diagonal form of the Hamiltonian and construct the physical Bogoliubov quasiparticle operators, confirming the equivalence of the new method to existing solutions.
method: The core technique involves casting the Hamiltonian into a quadratic form, solving the associated non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem using an asymmetric plane-wave ansatz, and resolving the resulting degeneracies via bosonic commutation relations.
model_or_system: The system is the bosonic Kitaev chain with open boundary conditions, treated as an effective Hamiltonian for a driven-dissipative open system. The analysis is generalized to other bosonic pairing models with inhomogeneous terms.
key_observables: Eigenvalues (single-particle energies, $\Lambda_k$), eigenvectors ($V_j(\alpha)$), and the diagonalized Hamiltonian ($H_D$).
important_parameters: Number of sites ($N$), hopping strength ($t$), pairing strength ($\Delta$), and the pseudo-momenta ($p, p'$).
main_assumptions:
The primary assumption is the validity of the asymmetric plane-wave ansatz for solving the left eigenvalue problem, and the method assumes $\Lambda 
eq 0$ for the main derivation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the allowed values of the parameter $\alpha$ for finite $N$, showing the existence of a zero mode for odd $N$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reviewing the problem, then developing the algebraic framework using the asymmetric plane-wave ansatz to solve the eigenvalue problem, deriving the quantization conditions, and finally constructing the diagonal Hamiltonian and generalizing the method to inhomogeneous pairing models.
why_interesting: The method provides a powerful, purely algebraic tool for exactly solving non-Hermitian Hamiltonians arising in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding boundary effects in condensed matter models.
